Svalbard, Norway ❄️

Between 74° and 82° north, this remote Arctic archipelago is home to the world’s northernmost hotel, supermarket, cinema, library and kebab van.

❄️ Even Norwegians need a passport to visit: Svalbard is outside Schengen.
❄️ Outside settlements, people carry firearms for protection from polar bears; guns are banned in town.
❄️ About 2,500 people and 3,000 polar bears live here.
❄️ Seven of Norway’s 47 national parks are here; 60% of the territory is protected.
❄️ An Arctic desert, Svalbard is warmer and wetter than before. Vegetation covers under 10% of the islands.
❄️ Winter auroras can appear by day; October and February bring vivid blue light.
❄️ Burials stopped in the 1950s because permafrost slows decomposition. Expectant mothers travel to mainland Norway to give birth.
❄️ The 1925 Svalbard Treaty lets anyone live here without a visa—but offers no shortcut to mainland Norwegian residency.

📄 Iran holds 2nd Persian Language Proficiency Test

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The second session of the Persian Language Proficiency Test (Parsik) has been held at four domestic and international examination centers, says a deputy of the minister of science, research, and technology.

Saeed Habiba said on Friday that non-Persian-speaking students seeking to study at Iranian universities must complete the required Persian language training.
​
The test took place Friday morning, with about 200 non-Persian-speaking students participating. The examination took place at four centers: Ferdowsi University of Mashhad, Razi University in Kermanshah, Allameh Tabataba’i University, and the University of Tehran’s International Campus in Baghdad.
​
Habiba added that the Persian Language Proficiency Test is administered to ensure international students have the language skills required to study at Iranian universities, enabling them to understand and fully benefit from the educational content of their academic programs in Iran.
